newsitem.title: GREECE: GNN GUIDE: CAPITAL ADEQUACY RATIOS FOR COMMERCIAL BANKS.
newsitem.headline: GNN GUIDE: CAPITAL ADEQUACY RATIOS FOR COMMERCIAL BANKS.

text.p: We are giving a brief description of terms related to the calculation of minimum capital requirements for commercial banks based on the Basle agreement.
We are doing this because terms such as Tier-II capital have been coined in the past but many players say that they are not aware of what they are all about.
The minimum capital adequacy ratio for commercial banks is set by the Basle agreement at 8.0 percent.
Bank assets are weighted, that is multilied by a number from 0 to 1, and then are being added before the capital required to meet the minimum 8.0 percent ratio is determined.
There are five risk weights reflecting different probabilities of default, 0, 0.1, 0.20, 0.50, 1. There are four risk weights for interest rate and foreign exchange instruments.
An asset assigned a weight of 0 does not use any capital. Assets such as cash, bullion, loans to OECD governments and central banks belong to this category.

It should be noted that off-balance sheet items such as interest rate swaps are assigned risk weights as well as conversion factors. The factors are being multiplied by the risk weights to determine the final weight. For example, if the risk weight for the asset is 0.50 and the factor is 0.1 then their product, that is 0.05 (0.50x0.1), is being used to calculate risk capital requirements.
Market risk under the Basle agreement is being calculated based on one of the following two methods:
1) The current exposure method which calculates present and future market risk in the form of replacement cost and residual maturity weights.
2) The original exposure method using fixed weights expressed as percentages of principal amounts related to the original maturity of the instrument.

1) CORE or TIER-I CAPITAL which includes common stock valued at par, perpetual preferred stock, minirity interest in consolidated subsidiaries, retained earnings and others. Treasury stock and goodwill are being substracted from the above items.

2) SUPPLEMENTAL or TIER-II CAPITAL: Limited-life preferred stock, loan-loss reserves, perpetual debt, mandatory convertible securiites and subordianted debt with an original maturity of not less than five years.
The state National Bank of Greece said it would issue a $200 to $250 million subordinated loan (Tier-II) to increase its capital base. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
